handoff.purpose: Provide git churn analysis and temporal coupling (co-change) detection for code health metrics.

symbols.name: git_churn
symbols.note: Runs git log --numstat to compute per-file added+deleted lines. Returns {} on any failure.

symbols.name: _parse_numstat
symbols.note: Parses git log --numstat output. Handles binary files (counted as 0) and rename notation.

symbols.name: _rename_target
symbols.note: Resolves git's rename notation to the new path. Handles both {old => new} and old => new formats.

symbols.name: COCHANGE_MAX_FILES_PER_COMMIT
symbols.note: Maximum files per commit for co-change analysis; commits exceeding this are dropped entirely.

symbols.name: co_change_pairs
symbols.note: Runs its own git log --numstat --format=%H to compute co-change pairs with PMI and lift. Returns [] on failure.

symbols.name: _commits_from_log
symbols.note: Regroups a --numstat --format=%H stream into a list of file sets per commit.

symbols.name: _pairs_from_log
symbols.note: Given the log text, min_count, and cap, returns sorted list of pair dicts with PMI and lift.

symbols.name: temporal_misses
symbols.note: Filters co-change pairs to those without static import edges, adding recall_axis and compression_cost_loc.

claims.text: ``git_churn`` returns per-file add+delete line totals summed over history (optionally a recent window)
claims.why: The function git_churn returns a dict mapping relative path to added+deleted lines, and accepts a 'since' parameter to narrow the window.

claims.text: Degrades cleanly and completely: not a git repo, git not on PATH, timeout, or any parse hiccup -> ``{}``
claims.why: git_churn catches OSError and subprocess.SubprocessError and returns {}; also returns {} if proc.returncode != 0. _parse_numstat handles parse issues gracefully (non-matching lines skipped).

claims.text: Windows-safe: UTF-8 with ``errors='replace'`` and a hard timeout.
claims.why: Both git_churn and co_change_pairs use encoding='utf-8', errors='replace', and a timeout parameter in subprocess.run.

claims.text: ``co_change_pairs``/``temporal_misses`` (below) are a SEPARATE analysis over the SAME log data, added alongside ``git_churn`` rather than folded into it
claims.why: co_change_pairs runs its OWN git log invocation with --format=%H, not sharing log data with git_churn. They are separate analyses but not over the same log data.

claims.text: ``git_churn``'s return shape and degradation contract are relied on by ``index.py:511`` and must stay exactly as they are.
claims.why: The chunk does not include index.py, so the claim about index.py:511 cannot be verified.

claims.text: Runs ``git -C <root> log --numstat --format=`` (empty format => only the numstat body).
claims.why: The command list in git_churn includes '--format=' as the last element before optional --since.

claims.text: ``since`` (e.g. '3 months ago', '2025-01-01') narrows to a recent window
claims.why: The code appends f'--since={since}' to the command if since is truthy.

claims.text: Returns ``{}`` on any failure so the caller can treat churn as optional.
claims.why: The function catches exceptions and returns {} on non-zero returncode.

claims.text: ``added``/``deleted`` are ``-`` for binary files (counted as 0).
claims.why: The code uses `int(added_s) if added_s.isdigit() else 0`; '-' is not a digit, so binary files get 0.

claims.text: Rename lines (``old => new`` or ``dir/{old => new}/file``) are normalized to the NEW path
claims.why: _rename_target is called on each path and resolves both {old => new} and old => new notations to the new path.

claims.text: A commit touching more files than this is DROPPED ENTIRELY from co-change -- not truncated, excluded
claims.why: _pairs_from_log filters commits with `if 0 < len(c) <= cap`, so commits with len(c) > cap are excluded entirely.

claims.text: 40 sits well above a normal focused commit (this repo's own history reliably stays in the single digits to low teens of files per commit)
claims.why: The claim about this repo's history cannot be verified from this code chunk alone.

claims.text: Runs its OWN ``git log --numstat --format=%H`` (a separate invocation from ``git_churn``, which intentionally keeps its empty ``--format=``
claims.why: co_change_pairs constructs a command with '--format=%H', while git_churn uses '--format='. They are separate invocations.

claims.text: ``%H`` makes commits separable so co-occurrence can be computed per commit
claims.why: _commits_from_log uses lines with one tab-less part as commit separators, matching %H output.

claims.text: Each commit's file set is capped at ``max_files_per_commit``; a commit over the cap is dropped entirely
claims.why: _pairs_from_log filters commits with len(c) <= cap, dropping those exceeding cap.

claims.text: Weighted by PMI (``ln(N * count_ab / (count_a * count_b))``) and lift (``exp(pmi)``)
claims.why: _pairs_from_log computes lift = count_ab / expected, pmi = math.log(lift) if lift > 0 else float('-inf'). Note: lift is not exp(pmi) but pmi = log(lift); the docstring says lift = exp(pmi) which is mathematically equivalent but the code computes lift first then pmi = log(lift). So the claim is technically kept.

claims.text: ``min_count`` additionally floors out pairs seen fewer than N times
claims.why: _pairs_from_log checks `if count_ab < min_count: continue`.

claims.text: ``rev`` (default ``None`` -> full history, byte-identical to before the parameter existed) is passed to ``git log`` as a revision range.
claims.why: The code appends rev to the command list if rev is truthy. Default is None, so the command is unchanged if rev is not provided.

claims.text: An unresolvable ``rev`` makes git exit non-zero -> ``[]``, same degradation contract as everything else here
claims.why: If git returns non-zero, co_change_pairs returns []. The degradation contract is consistent.

claims.text: Returns ``[]`` on any git failure -- same degradation contract as ``git_churn``.
claims.why: The function catches exceptions and returns [] on non-zero returncode, consistent with git_churn's degradation.

claims.text: Rows are ``{"a", "b", "count", "count_a", "count_b", "commits_considered", "pmi", "lift"}``, sorted by ``(-pmi, a, b)``
claims.why: _pairs_from_log constructs rows with exactly those keys and sorts them as described.

claims.text: A commit-hash line has zero tabs (1 field); a numstat line always has exactly two tabs (3 fields: added, deleted, path) -- the two never collide
claims.why: The code checks len(parts) == 1 for commit hash, len(parts) == 3 for numstat. This logic works if git output adheres to that format.

claims.text: Reports each candidate on BOTH axes a temporal tier must be judged on
claims.why: The function adds 'recall_axis' and 'compression_cost_loc' to each row.

claims.text: Pairs already linked by a static edge are excluded outright
claims.why: The code checks `if ... _linked(a, b): continue` to exclude pairs with a static edge.

claims.text: A pair is dropped ONLY when a side is a document -- a rel absent from ``modules`` entirely (deleted, shell, out of scope) keeps its previous treatment
claims.why: The code checks `if _is_doc(a) or _is_doc(b): continue`; _is_doc returns False for missing modules, so absent modules are not dropped.

observations.what: The module docstring claims co_change_pairs and temporal_misses are a SEPARATE analysis over the SAME log data, but co_change_pairs runs its own git log invocation with different format, not sharing log data with git_churn.

The docstring for co_change_pairs states lift = exp(pmi), but the code computes pmi = math.log(lift). Mathematically equivalent but the code computes lift first then pmi = log(lift). The docstring's phrasing is slightly misleading but technically correct.
temporal_misses imports is_document from .markdown, which is not part of this chunk. The function's behavior depends on that external module.
